parts.label: Part I
parts.title: Before the code
parts.intro: What zram needs from a codec, how LZ compression and Huffman codes work, what makes code slow on a CPU, and the seqlz format on one page. Read this part first if you have never written a compressor or kernel code.

parts.label: Part II
parts.title: Level 1: an LZ with Huffman coded sequences
parts.intro: The code of src/ that level 1 has, file by file, with a short note next to each block, and under a note the details when you want them: why, a worked example, what it was measured at. Level 1 keeps the literals as they are; a build with SEQLZ_LEVELS=1 is this code and nothing else. Where a file has lines of levels 2 and 3, one line says which and links to them. The map comes first, then the files in the order of the contents.

parts.label: Part III
parts.title: Level 2: coded literals
parts.intro: What level 2 adds to level 1: the literals Huffman coded with one of 8 fixed tables, where that saves enough. The literal coder and decoder are files of their own; the other files get a few lines each, the hooks where level 2 joins level 1's code.

parts.label: Part IV
parts.title: Level 3: a lazy matcher, deltas, a table of the page's own
parts.intro: What level 3 adds to level 2: a lazy step and a step back in the matcher, the literals as deltas to earlier bytes of the page, and a literal table of the page's own where that saves more. Most of it is a block at the end of the literal coder and its decoder; the other files get the hooks.

parts.label: Part V
parts.title: The whole picture
parts.intro: One page followed through every function, and the design decisions with the measurements behind them.
